scenarios.title: Explain a checkout bug to a developer
scenarios.context: You’re in a team stand-up. You found a reproducible problem on the checkout page. Explain what happens, how you reproduced it, and what you expected instead.
scenarios.colleaguePrompt: Hi Anna, I saw your ticket about checkout. Can you walk me through the issue and tell me what happens after the user clicks Pay?
scenarios.sampleResponse: The checkout page crash when I click Pay. Yesterday I reproduce the issue on Chrome and Safari. The user see an error message, and the payment don't go through. I expected the order to complete, but the page stay on loading.

simulatedFeedback.opening: Your explanation is understandable and includes the trigger, impact, and expected behaviour.

items.title: Recurring pattern detected: verb forms
items.copy: This pattern has now appeared 7 times across recent practice scenarios. Prioritise a short review before the next conversation.
pairs: The page stays on the loading screen

items.title: More precise system-state language
items.copy: Your meaning is clear. More precise QA language could make the report easier to act on.
pairs: the loading spinner remains visible / the page remains stuck in a loading state

items.title: Make the report easy to scan
items.copy: Try structuring the explanation as: Steps to reproduce → Actual result → Expected result.

scenarios.title: Report a file-upload issue
scenarios.context: A user uploads a PDF larger than 10 MB. The progress bar reaches 100%, but the file never appears in the document list. Explain the problem to a developer and say what you expected to happen.
scenarios.sampleResponse: When the user uploads a PDF larger than 10 MB, the progress bar reaches 100%, but the file does not appear in the document list. I reproduced the issue twice in Chrome. I expected the file to appear after the upload completed.

simulatedResult.headline: Improvement detected in this sample.
simulatedResult.feedback: Your verb forms are accurate in this response, and the sequence of events is easy to follow.
simulatedResult.secondarySuggestion: For even more precise QA language, you could say: ‘The upload completes, but the document is not saved to the list.’
simulatedResult.statusMessage: EN-QA-GRAM-001 is improving. Recheck the skill in two more job-specific scenarios before considering it stable.

practiceActivities.title: Verb Forms for Reporting Software Issues
practiceActivities.description: Practise the verb forms you need to describe reproducible software behaviour clearly.

items.stem: The checkout page ___ every time the user clicks Pay.
items.feedback: Correct. ‘The checkout page’ is third-person singular, so the present-simple verb takes -s.

items.stem: Yesterday, I ___ the issue on two browsers.
items.feedback: Correct. ‘Yesterday’ signals a completed past event, so use the past simple.

items.stem: The user ___ an error message after submitting the form.
items.feedback: Correct. ‘The user’ is singular, so use ‘sees’.

items.stem: The payment ___ go through after the timeout.
items.feedback: Correct. Use ‘doesn’t’ with the singular subject ‘the payment’.

items.stem: The page ___ on the loading screen until the user refreshes it.
items.feedback: Correct. We are describing reproducible current behaviour, so use the present simple.
